subject.title: [voice-call] OpenAI realtime: audio clipping / breaking inside words during first ~30s of outbound calls (Twilio mulaw output)

question: Should maintainers sponsor a live Twilio/OpenAI Voice Call diagnosis now, and should the first sponsored path be instrumentation, gain/codec adjustment, or pacing/prewarm work?
rationale: The report is credible, but the current evidence does not isolate whether the failure is provider audio format, mulaw level, resampling, Twilio pacing, or call-start buffering; a blind fix would change shared realtime phone audio.

options.title: Live diagnose first
options.body: Run a controlled outbound Twilio/OpenAI call with redacted audio and output-level diagnostics, then choose the smallest proven fix.

options.title: Add bounded diagnostics
options.body: Add maintainer-approved level, queue, and underrun telemetry first so operators can gather evidence without changing audio behavior.

options.title: Defer until artifact
options.body: Keep the issue open but wait for the reporter or maintainer to provide a current audio sample or packet capture before implementation.

recommendation.title: Live diagnose first
recommendation.body: Run a controlled outbound Twilio/OpenAI call with redacted audio and output-level diagnostics, then choose the smallest proven fix.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest current routing candidate from codec work and current-line history on the implicated pacer/codec paths.
